title: Module 8 Misconception Sort
intro: Decide whether each statement is true, false, or depends. These are the misconceptions that cost students points on exams.

items.s: An independent-measures t test can be used when the same people are measured twice.
items.why: Repeated measurements on the same people are related. Use a related-samples test.

items.s: Equal sample sizes make the pooled variance simply the average of the two sample variances.
items.why: With n1 equal to n2, the weights are equal.

items.s: A significant independent t test shows which specific people benefited from the treatment.
items.why: It tests a difference between group means, not individual responses.

items.s: If both groups are large, the assumption of equal variances no longer matters.
items.why: Equal n and similar variances protect the test, but with unequal n and very different variances the Type I error rate can be off even with large groups.

items.s: The t statistic compares the mean difference with the amount of difference expected by sampling error.
items.why: It is a signal to noise ratio.

items.s: A big mean difference guarantees a significant t.
items.why: Large variability or small samples can make the standard error large enough to hide the difference.

items.s: Two groups with the same mean must have the same variance.
items.why: Mean and variance are separate properties of a distribution.

items.s: A study can show a large effect (d near .9) and still not reach significance.
items.why: Small samples can produce a large d with a large standard error.
